$comment: DRAFT schema fragments for the v0.5 proposal — NOT part of any published spec. STATUS: P035 speakers { name, url?, sameAs?, type? } — sameAs added to CORE at hhkaos's call (R10), over Codex's R9 recommendation to keep it in P038, same override pattern as recordings; P036 recordings; P037 pricing (Model A, breaking 0.5.0); P038 extensions page (speakers affiliation/jobTitle/bio/image stay here, per-subfield status); P039 feed.alternates (#25); P040 contributing (#26). All into v0.5. Reproduce: node proposals/validate-fragments.mjs.

event.properties.speakers.description: Who gives the talk(s) — NOT who runs the event (that is organizers) and NOT where the data came from (source). A list in DISPLAY / preference order (first survives to single-value destinations), the same rule organizers and image state. Co-talks and panels are normal. Kept as small as organizers: a name, optionally where to find them. One document is one occurrence, so in a multipart conference the speakers of a given talk live on that talk's document, not on the parent. Only exact repeats are rejected; distinct entries are never deduplicated by inferred identity.

event.properties.recordings.description: Published recordings of the event, added AFTER it happened (same id, new updatedAt). NOT location.onlineUrl (the live link) and NOT image (the poster). A list — a talk may be on more than one platform, or split into parts.

partOf.properties.offers.description: P037. The shared admission price of a multipart set, written identically on every part so a consumer holding one part document can price it without resolving the parent. Reuses $defs/offers verbatim. IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: adopting this also requires updating four other rule sites so partOf.offers[].translations is policed like every other nested translations map — the base textLanguage requirement enumeration, the distinctTranslationLanguages keyword, the D030 offers[].name warning, generated reference paths, and the invalid-example corpus. Accepted cost (breaking changes are on the table).

offer.properties.scope.description: P037. What this offer entry means relative to the set's shared admission (partOf.offers). Only meaningful when the document has partOf. `admission` (what an absent scope is read as): a complete way to attend this part — sold standalone, or a restatement of the set admission. `add-on`: an ADDITIONAL charge on top of the set admission; total = a priced partOf.offers entry + this entry's price WHEN BOTH carry a number, otherwise 'additional charge, total unknown' (URL-only offers are valid — v0.4 allows price-or-url). The schema enforces `if any offer scope == 'add-on' then partOf AND partOf.offers are required`. Recommended-tier warns if scope 'add-on' is present but no partOf.offers entry has a price. `admission` covers ALL admission tiers; 'this add-on only applies to the Pro tier' is OUT OF SCOPE for v0.5 (Model B).

feed.properties.alternates.description: P039 (#25). feed.schema.json only. Where this same collection is published in other formats (RSS, iCalendar, schema.org JSON-LD). The JSON form of an HTML <link rel='alternate'> / the Link: HTTP header, for feeds with no HTML page. INFORMATIONAL — OTE does not guarantee the linked resources are generated from this feed or kept in sync with it.

event.$defs.contributing.$comment: P040 (#26). Round 7: a SHARED $def in spec/v0.5/event.schema.json#/$defs — the feed schema $refs it cross-schema by $id, exactly as feed.license/textLanguage/updatedAt do. Round 8: accepts an HTTP(S) IRI OR a mailto: URI (real producer dev.events points at hello@dev.events). A mailto: carries the SAME role-address discipline as organizers[].email: a role address (hello@, corrections@), never someone's personal mailbox, and never populated from a non-public source.

anyOf.description: An HTTP(S) IRI — an issue tracker, a form, an OTE editor deep link (?repo=...).
A mailto: URI with ONE bare role address — no headers (?...), no second recipient (,), no fragment (#), and no raw RFC 6068 gen-delims (/ [ ]) that the RFC says must be percent-encoded.

feed.properties.contributing.description: P040 (#26). URL for reporting or proposing a data change in this feed's records. The default every event inherits when it omits its own (default-value inheritance, like license — a declared scalar replaces the inherited one). Exists because an aggregator must omit organizers and source.url points upstream, not at the aggregator's copy.

event.properties.contributing.description: P040 (#26). URL for reporting or proposing a data change in this record — including an aggregator's own mapping error. Inherited from feed.contributing unless declared here. Like cfp it travels to no destination format; its value is inside the OTE ecosystem (a reading tool's 'suggest a correction' button). NOT recommended-tier.

documentConstraints.$comment: P037. Added to the standalone-event top-level allOf AND to $defs/event (so it also applies to feed-embedded events). An add-on charge is meaningless without the set admission it sits on top of, and the add-on total is only computable when partOf.offers is present IN THE SAME DOCUMENT (resolving partOf.id -> parent is not relied on). So: any offer with scope 'add-on' requires partOf AND partOf.offers.

feedRootKeywords.$comment: P037. Same mechanism/rationale as D011 uniqueEventIds — only the feed root sees sibling documents. NEEDS ITS OWN DECISIONS.md ENTRY because the equality relation is over nested JSON, not one id string.

sharedOffersConsistent.rule: For every group of feed events sharing a partOf.id, the partOf.offers arrays that ARE present must be equal by value. Events in the group that omit partOf.offers are allowed (a part may be described before its price is set); WARNING if some siblings carry it and others do not, once P037's recommended-profile pricing-completeness check exists.
sharedOffersConsistent.equality: Array order is significant (offers are an ordered list, like image[] and organizers[]). Object member order is NOT significant, including inside a nested translations map. Numeric equality is JSON-value equality (45 === 45.0). String equality is exact (no case folding, no URI normalisation) — same discipline as D011. null is treated as absent ({price: null} === {}).
sharedOffersConsistent.referenceImpl: proposals/validate-fragments.mjs has deepEqualJson + sharedOffersConsistent and four feed-level test cases (identical with swapped member order -> consistent; differing price -> inconsistent; array order differs -> inconsistent; one sibling omits -> allowed).
sharedOffersConsistent.fallback: If a hard feed-root error is judged too heavy: a recommended-tier warning instead. It must not be left undefined.

mediaType.description: IANA media type of the alternate representation. A loose shape check, not a closed list.

url.description: Absolute HTTP(S) IRI of the alternate representation. No embedded credentials.

name.description: Display name of the speaker. A proper noun: never translated.

url.description: The speaker's canonical page — their own site, or their main profile. One URL. Same rules as organizers[].url. For OTHER profiles, use sameAs.

sameAs.description: R9/R10. Other profile pages for this SAME person — Mastodon, LinkedIn, GitHub, a personal site distinct from `url`. A list; order not significant; only exact repeats rejected. Maps to schema.org Person.sameAs (identity reconciliation). NOTE: Google's Event rich-result docs do not document nested performer.sameAs — the value is generic schema.org consumers and OTE-ecosystem directories, not a Google rich result. URLs, so no translation.

type.description: Person or organisation. A translator picks a schema.org @type either way, and Person is the tolerant choice for a speaker.

url.description: Absolute HTTP(S) IRI where the recording can be watched. A watch page (YouTube, PeerTube) is fine here — unlike image, this does not have to be the media file itself.

title.description: What this recording is, when the list has more than one ('Q&A', 'Full session'). Noise when there is only one. Free text, in the document's textLanguage; translated by this entry's own translations map.

translations.description: This recording's title in other languages. Local to the entry, never a positional mirror. Requires the document's textLanguage; policed by the same rules as image[].translations (D010/D023/D030).

suggestedExtensions.$comment: P038. NON-NORMATIVE recommended shapes for the suggested-extensions page — NOT part of any schema, NOT validated. Each sub-field is its own registry entry with independent adoption count + status. speakers[].sameAs moved to the P035 CORE (R10). event.sameAs (below) stays here on purpose: it steps into 'deduplication across sources', a stated non-goal.

registryEntry.name: sameAs
registryEntry.graduationQuestion: ≥2 aggregators emit it pointing at a shared canonical URL, AND the 'dedup out of scope' non-goal is revisited (publisher hint vs heuristic).

event-sameAs.$comment: URLs the publisher asserts describe the SAME event (organiser's canonical page, another OTE id, a well-known listing). Publisher assertion, NOT a consumer heuristic. Maps to schema.org Event.sameAs. Distinct from `id` (per-publisher stable identifier, for updates) and from `source.url` (provenance — 'I got this from here', already required for aggregated events).

speakers-enrichment.note: These are suggested-extension shapes. A translations map that appears inside one of them (e.g. speakers[].image[].translations) is NOT policed by the core D010/D023/D030 keywords — those enumerate a fixed set of sites and would only cover speakers[].* after a future normative adoption.

affiliation.$comment: ONE organisation DISPLAY name, written once — a proper noun, not translated. Same 'choose the audience-recognisable spelling once' rule as organizers[].name and the locality-spellings note in the README. Maps to schema.org Person.affiliation (Organization by name).

registryEntry.name: speakers[].jobTitle
registryEntry.graduationQuestion: ≥3 producers, AND worth the translations-map cost?

jobTitle.$comment: free text, in the document's textLanguage. Maps to schema.org Person.jobTitle. Graduation touches D010/D023/D030 (needs a local translations map).

bio.$comment: free text prose, in the document's textLanguage. Maps to schema.org Person.description.

registryEntry.name: speakers[].image
registryEntry.graduationQuestion: ≥3 producers, AND worth reopening the image[].alt apparatus nested in speakers[]?

image.$comment: SAME shape as event image[] ($defs/images) — a string or { url, alt, translations }. Highest cost. speakers[].image[].translations is NOT core-validated as an extension (see the note above).
